name: Keren-Happuch
title: Job's youngest daughter
summary: Keren-Happuch was the youngest of Job's three daughters born after God restored his prosperity. Her name means 'horn of antimony' and suggests great beauty. Together with her sisters, she was counted among the most beautiful women in the land, and she received an inheritance from her father equal to that of her brothers.

keyEvents.title: Job's restoration
keyEvents.description: After Job's great suffering and trials, God restored his prosperity and gave him twice as much as he had before. He also received new children, including Keren-Happuch.

keyEvents.title: The naming of Job's daughters
keyEvents.description: Keren-Happuch was named the third and youngest of Job's new daughters, after Jemimah and Keziah. Her name, meaning 'horn of antimony,' suggests beauty and prosperity.

keyEvents.title: The most beautiful women in the land
keyEvents.description: The Bible highlights that there were no more beautiful women than Job's three daughters anywhere in the land, underscoring God's rich blessing upon Job.

keyEvents.title: Inheritance equal to their brothers
keyEvents.description: Job gave Keren-Happuch and her sisters an inheritance along with their brothers, which was very unusual in the ancient Near East and demonstrated Job's justice and generosity.

keyEvents.title: Job's Blessed Old Age
keyEvents.description: After his restoration, Job lived another 140 years and saw his descendants through four generations, including the offspring of Keren-Happuch.
